1.note: Zechariah is using the word translated as **And it happened** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Here Zechariah is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

The name **Zechariah** refers to the prophet himself, who also narrates this book in the first person. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the word of Yahweh came to me, Zechariah]

If your language would not represent numbers in a form such as **fourth** and **ninth**, you could represent these numbers in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [on day four of month nine]

The **Kislev** month of the Hebrew calendar includes parts of November and December on Western calendars. You could convert the Hebrew day and month into an approximate date on the calendar that your culture uses. However, the Jews used a lunar calendar, so if you use a solar calendar, the date will be different every year, and the translation will not be entirely accurate. So you may just want to give the number of the day and the name of the month on the Hebrew calendar and say in a footnote approximately what time of year that is on your calendar.

2.note: Here, **Bethel** represents the people who lived in that city. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [The people who lived in Bethel]
The words **Sharezer and Regem-Melech** are the names of men.
The pronoun **their** refers to Sharezer and Regem-Melech. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the men who were with them]

Here, **the face of Yahweh** represents his presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the presence of Yahweh]

3.note: The pronoun **I** refers to the people of Bethel collectively, speaking through their envoys. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Should we mourn in the fifth month by means of a fast, as we have done these many years]

Here Zechariah is speaking of the temple as if it were a **house** in which Yahweh lived. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [at the temple where Yahweh of hosts lives]

3.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֗ר אֶל־הַ⁠כֹּֽהֲנִים֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ לְ⁠בֵית־יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וְ⁠אֶל־הַ⁠נְּבִיאִ֖ים לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר הַֽ⁠אֶבְכֶּה֙ בַּ⁠חֹ֣דֶשׁ הַ⁠חֲמִשִׁ֔י הִנָּזֵ֕ר כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתִי זֶ֖ה כַּ⁠מֶּ֥ה שָׁנִֽים
3.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [They asked the priests who were at the house of Yahweh of hosts and the prophets whether they should mourn in the fifth month by means of a fast, as they had done for many years]

5.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and ask them if when you fasted]
The word **you** is plural here because Yahweh is addressing all the people of the land and the priests, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke the people for fasting for their own benefit rather than truly honoring him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [you were not truly fasting for me.]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **fasting** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [were you truly fasting for me]

6.note: The word **you** is plural here because Yahweh is continuing to address all the people of the land and the priests, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that the people were eating and drinking for their own benefit. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [you ate and drank only for yourselves.]

7.note: Yahweh is using the question form to remind the people that these are the same messages he gave through the earlier prophets. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [These were the same words that Yahweh proclaimed]

The next verse clarifies that the pronoun **these** refers to the messages about justice and mercy that Yahweh had proclaimed through the earlier prophets. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Were these messages about justice and mercy not the same words that]

Here, **by the hand of the former prophets** represents the words that the prophets spoke. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [by what the former prophets said]

7.q: בִּ⁠הְי֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ יֹשֶׁ֣בֶת וּ⁠שְׁלֵוָ֔ה וְ⁠עָרֶ֖י⁠הָ סְבִיבֹתֶ֑י⁠הָ
7.note: Zechariah is using the clause **when you still inhabited Jerusalem and the surrounding cities in prosperity** to describe something that was ongoing. This provides the background for the prophetic messages that Yahweh proclaimed during this time. Connect this clause to the story in a way that makes it clear in your language that this clause is describing something that was ongoing in the background. Alternate translation: [while you were still living in Jerusalem and the surrounding cities in prosperity and were settled in the Negev, and the foothills to the west]

The expression **were settled** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and had settled in the Negev]

8.note: Zechariah is using the phrase **The word of Yahweh came** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

9.note: The word from Yahweh in verses 9-14 are providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

9.q: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר מִשְׁפַּ֤ט אֱמֶת֙ שְׁפֹ֔טוּ
9.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh of Armies commands you to judge with true justice]

The phrase **saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this phrase explicitly.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **justice**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [rightly]

The terms **covenant faithfulness** and **mercy** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [and steadfast love]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [be faithful to what you agreed]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **mercy**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and be merciful]

Here the masculine terms **man** and **his brother** have a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [Let each person do this for one another]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if each fellow Israelite were **his brother**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for his fellow Israelite]

10.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **evil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and … anything harmful]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if people’s thoughts and intentions were located in their **heart**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in your thoughts]

11.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the ancestors of the people Yahweh is currently addressing, not to the current audience. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [But their ancestors refused]

Here Zechariah is speaking of the people as if they were stubborn animals that **gave a stubborn shoulder** and refused to be led. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and refused to be led or directed]

Here Zechariah is speaking as if their **ears were heavy** so that they could not hear. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Their ears were closed to hearing] or [They would not listen]

12.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **rock** is hard and unyielding, so were the people’s hearts resistant to Yahweh’s commands. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [They hardened their hearts and made them unwilling to obey]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **the law**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what God commanded]
See how you translated this same phrase in Zechariah 7:7. Alternate translation: [through the words of the prophets]

13.note: The pronoun **he** refers to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh called]

13.q: וְ⁠לֹ֣א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ כֵּ֤ן יִקְרְאוּ֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א אֶשְׁמָ֔ע
13.note: The first pronoun **they** refer to the ancestors who refused to listen in the past, the second refers to any future hearers. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the ancestors did not listen, so when their descendants call I will not listen]

The phrases translated as **as when … so** indicates that what follows is a result that mirrors what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a consequence of what came before. Alternate translation: [So because when he called, they did not listen, they will call out to me, but I will not answer]

14.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of his judgment as if it were **a whirlwind** that scatters people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [For I violently scattered them]
The pronoun **them** refers to the Israelites whom Yahweh has scattered. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [after the Israelites are gone]

Yahweh is referring to all human activity in the land by naming two major components, **pass through** and **returning**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [For no one will ever be in the land again]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **land of desire** that is characterized by being desirable. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the desirable land]
